work_order.understanding:
Issue #98 collects five non-blocking findings the review of PR #95 (for #92) approved despite, and instructs me to check each still reproduces, drop any that does not, and split the ticket if the findings turn out to be unrelated. I reproduced all five against the current tree by reading the code; none has been fixed since the review wrote it.

Finding 1 (ReportCard.tsx:165, the click guard) and finding 3 (the same lines, the keydown guard) are one defect seen twice, not two: the click guard resolves `target.closest(INTERACTIVE_SELECTOR)` (eleven entries, ReportCard.tsx:25-37) while the keydown guard four lines below returns on `e.target !== e.currentTarget`, which is every descendant unconditionally. The comment above explains why the click guard cannot use target identity, but never says the two therefore cover different sets. They do: a `tabIndex={0}` descendant navigates the card on click and is swallowed on Enter.

The reviewer's evidence that this is not live today is incomplete in a way that changes the fix. It rests on `grep -rn "tabIndex" packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/reports/` returning nothing, but that path excludes `graphs/`. `ReportTable.tsx:154` does render `<View tabIndex={0}>` — the keyboard-scrolling container around the report table's rows — and it is reachable inside a card that carries a `to`: `CustomReportListCards.tsx:133-137` renders `ReportCard to={/reports/custom/${report.id}}`, whose body is `GetCardData` (line 163), which renders `ChooseGraph` (GetCardData.tsx:188-192), which renders `ReportTable` for `graphType === 'TableGraph'` (ChooseGraph.tsx:189-191). A custom-report widget whose graph is a table therefore has a focusable non-activatable descendant inside its clickable card today. That makes the reviewer's primary fix — and its own fallback, since both add `[tabindex]` — a live behaviour change: every click inside that table's scroll container would stop navigating the card. The e2e would not catch it (`goToBalanceForecastPage` clicks a LineChart card whose body has no tabIndex).

Finding 2 (`a[href]` at ReportCard.tsx:30) reproduces as written and is unreachable: no card body renders an anchor, and MarkdownCard — the only card that renders markdown, the only way an anchor could appear via rehypeExternalLinks — passes no `to` (MarkdownCard.tsx:101-106) and so never installs this handler. The selector encodes a decision that no acceptance criterion and no comment states.

Finding 4 reproduces exactly: three copies of one idiom. `grep -rln "from 'node:fs'" packages/desktop-client/src/` returns ReportCard.test.tsx, useDashboardWidget.test.tsx and useReport.test.tsx and nothing else. The first factors it into `readOwnSource` (ReportCard.test.tsx:120-124); the other two inline the identical `readFileSync` + strip-`//` + collapse-whitespace block (useDashboardWidget.test.tsx:143-148, useReport.test.tsx:136-141). `#mocks/*` is already mapped in packages/desktop-client/package.json and `src/mocks/connection.ts` already sets the precedent for a test-only module there.

Finding 5 reproduces. `error` and `fetchStatus` are the two fields the hook returns keep, and the comment above the return explains only why `status`, `isSuccess` and `isInitialLoading` go. Grepping every call site: twelve callers destructure `data` plus one of `isPending`/`isLoading`, and CustomReport.tsx:122 reads `data` and `isPending`; none reads `error`. `fetchStatus` has no production reader either (the only hit outside the two hooks is an unrelated literal in PayeeAutocomplete.test.tsx:137) — but the two hook tests read it at useReport.test.tsx:101 and useDashboardWidget.test.tsx:97, and it is the un-derived input of the derived `isPending`, so it earns its place for a reason `error` never had.

Split judgement: findings 1-3 are one change in one file. Finding 4 is test plumbing and finding 5 is a two-line surface change in two other files. All five are follow-ups to one merged PR, all in packages/desktop-client, and all land in one PR with one release note. Splitting would cost three CI and QA cycles for about sixty changed lines, so I am keeping them together — which is also what the issue's own framing ("one ticket for the lot") asks for unless the findings are unrelated, and they are not.

I could not execute anything to confirm this empirically: dependencies are not installed in this checkout (`node_modules/.bin/vitest` and `packages/desktop-client/node_modules` are both absent), so every statement above is from reading the code and grepping the tree.
work_order.root_cause: The click guard on ReportCard's surface enumerates the element types it knows about (INTERACTIVE_SELECTOR) while the rule it enforces is a property of the element (a control the widget body rendered owns its own click). The two halves of the handler therefore answer the same question two different ways — closest() against a type list for a click, unconditional target inequality for a keypress — and the divergence is neither documented nor tested, so it will be discovered by whoever next renders a focusable control into a widget body. Alongside it, three test files carry three copies of one source-reading helper, and the two report hooks keep a return field with no reader while dropping eight others on a stated rule that does not cover the one it keeps.
work_order.approach:
Make the divergence explicit and pinned rather than silently rewritten, and decline the fix that would change behaviour on a shipped path.

1. ReportCard.tsx — keep the allowlist and the keydown guard exactly as they are; add the activatable types the list is missing (`[role="radio"]`, `[role="switch"]`, `[role="option"]`, `[role="menuitemcheckbox"]`, `[role="menuitemradio"]`, `[role="textbox"]`, `[role="combobox"]`, `[role="searchbox"]`, `[role="slider"]`, `[role="spinbutton"]`, `[role="treeitem"]`, `summary`); and rewrite the comment above the selector to state the invariant, state that the click guard's set is deliberately narrower than the keydown guard's because a click can start on static content while a keypress cannot, and say explicitly that focusability is therefore not the click guard's test — which is why `[tabindex]` is absent and why ReportTable's `tabIndex={0}` scroll container still navigates its card on click. `[tabindex]` is declined, not overlooked: adding it would stop card navigation inside every table-graph custom-report widget (the reachability chain is in `understanding`).

2. `a[href]` stays, and is now stated where a reader of the selector will find it, pinned by a test, and recorded in risks. A link inside a widget body owning its click is the same rule that keeps CalendarCard's month button's click; removing the entry would change nothing observable today and make the next link-bearing widget body wrong.

3. Extract the normalized source read into one helper at `src/mocks/source.ts`, exported through the existing `#mocks/*` mapping. All three test files call it and drop their `node:fs`/`node:path` imports, so the idiom exists in exactly one place.

4. The two hooks drop `error` (no reader, production or test) and keep `fetchStatus` (the un-derived input of the derived `isPending`, and what the disabled-query cases assert against). The comment above each return is rewritten to state one rule — the return is what a caller needs: the data, the derived loading flag, and the raw fetch status that derivation reads; everything react-query also exposes either disagrees with the derived flag or has no reader — instead of naming only the three fields that happen to be dropped. The existing comment-content assertions in the hook tests must still hold, so the rewritten comment keeps the tokens `isPending && isFetching` and `paused` and never regains the phrase `react-query's own isLoading definition`.

5. One `Maintenance` release note covering all of it.

risks: Declining the reviewer's suggested fix is the main judgement in this plan. `[tabindex]` is deliberately NOT added to INTERACTIVE_SELECTOR even though the reviewer's primary fix and its own fallback both call for it: ReportTable.tsx:154 renders `<View tabIndex={0}>` and is reachable inside a card carrying a `to` (CustomReportListCards.tsx:133-137 -> GetCardData at :163 -> GetCardData.tsx:188-192 -> ChooseGraph.tsx:189-191 for graphType TableGraph). Adding `[tabindex]` would stop a click anywhere inside a table-graph custom-report widget from navigating its card — a live behaviour change on a path the review measured as unreachable, and one the e2e would not catch because goToBalanceForecastPage clicks a LineChart card. The reviewer's evidence came from grepping components/reports/reports/, which excludes components/reports/graphs/. If a person disagrees and wants [tabindex] added anyway, it is a one-line change plus a browser check on a table-graph widget — but it should be a decision, not a follow-up comment.

The twelve newly added selector entries are not exercised by any widget body in the app today — no reports component renders role=radio, role=switch, role=option, role=menuitemcheckbox, role=menuitemradio, role=textbox, role=combobox, role=searchbox, role=slider, role=spinbutton, role=treeitem or summary (grep over packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports returns only the five roles already in the list). They are covered by unit cases only, so their coverage does not prove a user-facing path; that is the accepted cost of answering finding 1 without a behaviour change.

`[role="textbox"]` and `[role="combobox"]` are broader than they look: a widget body that renders a read-only ARIA textbox or combobox will now swallow card clicks on it. Nothing does today, but it is the same class of surprise finding 2 is about, which is why the rewritten comment has to say what the list means rather than leave it as a bare enumeration.

Keeping `a[href]` means an inner link owns its click and the card does not navigate. That is intended and pinned, and it is recorded here because no acceptance criterion in the shipped work order named it — the reviewer's complaint was that this trade was undocumented, and it now is, but the behaviour is unchanged from what shipped in PR #95.

Dropping `error` from the two hook returns is an API reduction with no reader to satisfy: if a future widget wants an error state it must add the field back. That is deliberate — the alternative is a field kept on a rationale that does not distinguish it from the eight already dropped.

Rewriting the return comments in both hooks is constrained by test assertions on their wording (the tokens `isPending && isFetching` and `paused`, and the absence of `react-query's own isLoading definition`). An implementer who paraphrases freely will fail those tests; the required tokens are named in each file's change.

No forbidden path is touched: no .sdlc/**, .github/**, .claude/**, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or packages/*/migrations entry is in files[]. No host is added that would make the app send data anywhere, so env.api_allowlist in .sdlc/config.yml needs no change.

Every claim about current behaviour is from reading the code and grepping the tree. The implementer should expect the first `yarn install` to be the first real check.
out_of_scope: Replacing the role="button" + tabIndex={0} surface with a real <Button>, or otherwise removing the nested-interactive shape the comment above the surface records. That would change the click target and accessible name the e2e selectors depend on, which the comment already says is a larger change than this one.

Turning recharts' accessibilityLayer on. It is off repo-wide and is what makes the divergence non-live for chart surfaces; enabling it would add tabIndex to chart nodes and change what finding 1 is about.

Removing the source-reading comment tests outright. The review called them the weakest thing in the diff and offered dropping the idiom as a council decision; the cases encode two decisions that were argued and are asserted for that reason, so this ticket deduplicates them rather than deleting them.
Dropping the `isLoading` alias the hooks return alongside `isPending` — five of the twelve call sites read it. Removing it is an API reduction no finding asked for.

Any change to the hook return's `isPending` derivation, or to the comment above it in either hook (useDashboardWidget.ts lines 20-31, useReport.ts lines 11-22). Only the comment above the return and the `error` line change.

Making the ReportTable scroll container stop the click itself (stopPropagation) rather than relying on the selector. That is the other way to resolve the divergence and it would put the burden on every widget body; the selector is the one place the rule lives today.
Reopening the [AI] prefix and PR-template handling for #95, and any change to how the release note is published.
work_order.confidence_rationale: Every file named was read in full and every claim about current behaviour is traceable to a line: the eleven selector entries, the keydown guard's unconditional return, the three copies of the source read (confirmed by grep returning exactly three files), the absence of any reader of `error` or `fetchStatus` across all twelve call sites plus CustomReport, and the CustomReportListCards -> GetCardData -> ChooseGraph -> ReportTable chain that makes `[tabindex]` a live behaviour change. alternatives_considered.approach: Take the reviewer's primary fix for findings 1 and 3 as written: invert the click guard to walk from e.target up to e.currentTarget and block whenever an element carries a focusability/interactivity signal, using matches(':any-link, button, input, [tabindex], [contenteditable], [role]') plus typeof el.onclick === 'function'.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It blocks on [tabindex] and on any [role], so it swallows the same clicks as the fallback — including ReportTable's tabIndex={0} scroll container inside a to-bearing card (CustomReportListCards -> GetCardData -> ChooseGraph, graphType TableGraph). That is a live behaviour change on a shipped path, uncovered by any e2e, for a ticket whose findings are all non-blocking follow-ups. The typeof el.onclick check is also dead code under React's synthetic event system, which attaches at the root and never sets a DOM onclick property.

alternatives_considered.approach: Take the reviewer's own fallback for findings 1 and 3: add [tabindex] to INTERACTIVE_SELECTOR plus the remaining common roles, and pin a tabIndex={0} descendant to the same outcome as its keydown.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Adding [tabindex] is the same live regression — the pin the reviewer asks for would be pinning today's bug as intended behaviour. The 'remaining common roles' half of that suggestion is kept, and the [tabindex] half is declined with the reachability chain written into risks.

alternatives_considered.approach: For finding 2, drop a[href] from INTERACTIVE_SELECTOR so a link inside a widget body falls through to the card.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It changes nothing observable today (no card body renders an anchor) and makes the next link-bearing widget body wrong: the link's own navigation and the card's would both fire. Keeping the entry and naming the trade — with a test and a risks line — is what the reviewer asked for and is the smaller change.

alternatives_considered.approach: For finding 2, keep a[href] and add only a risks line, with no test and no code change.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The reviewer's actual objection is that the trade is unstated in the file where the selector lives, and a reviewer reading only ReportCard.tsx would not see a ticket's risks list. The comment and the pinning test put it where the decision is made.

alternatives_considered.approach: For finding 5, drop both error and fetchStatus from the two hook returns and rewrite the two disabled-query assertions onto isPending.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: fetchStatus is the un-derived input the derived isPending is computed from (useDashboardWidget.ts:22), so a caller seeing isPending: false cannot otherwise tell a disabled query from one that resolved empty — and the disabled-query cases assert fetchStatus 'idle' precisely to prove the query never ran. Dropping error alone removes the field with no reader and no derivation role, which is the whole of the finding.

alternatives_considered.approach: For finding 5, keep all three fields and only extend the comment.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: That is defensible on its own terms, but error then stays on exactly the rationale the reviewer rejected — kept, alongside eight dropped fields, with no stated reason. Dropping it is a two-line change with no reader to break.

alternatives_considered.approach: For finding 4, put readNormalizedSource on #mocks (src/mocks.tsx) itself rather than a new #mocks/source module.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: src/mocks.tsx is the store-and-providers helper every test that renders under TestProviders imports; adding a node:fs dependency to it widens what that import costs. src/mocks/connection.ts is already the precedent for a focused test-only module under the same mapping.

alternatives_considered.approach: Split the ticket into three — ReportCard guards, the shared test helper, the hook return.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The issue asks for a split only if the findings are unrelated. Findings 1-3 are one change in one file; 4 and 5 are small and touch the same package; all five follow one merged PR and would land as one PR with one release note. Three tickets would mean three CI and QA cycles for roughly sixty changed lines. The judgement is recorded here so a human can overrule it.

alternatives_considered.approach: Drop the three source-reading comment tests instead of deduplicating them.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The review explicitly left this as a council decision rather than a review comment, and the cases encode two decisions that were argued (that isFirstLoad is not react-query's own isLoading definition; that the nested-interactive trade is deliberate). Deleting them is a different decision than deduplicating them, and it is not this ticket's to take.
